findings.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu serialization from BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource key to both pass the cache miss and race into bleve.New / builder writes, with the loser's cache entry silently overwritten. Concurrent index builds for the same key (previously prevented by the held lock for the whole build, which took seconds) now double-write the same bleve directory on disk (file-threshold path), causing bleve.New to fail with 'index already exists'/corrupt index errors, and whichever build finishes last clobbers the other's in-memory cache entry — events indexed into the discarded index are lost until the next rebuild.

[ADVISORY] The postgres path of TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is now unconditionally skipped in CI, and the skip is a TODO with no linked issue. Postgres integration coverage for the storage server silently disappears from Drone; regressions in the postgres path of this test's setup will only surface when someone runs locally, and the skip is untracked so it can persist indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) into NewResourceServer converts every per-request lazy initialization failure into a hard constructor failure, and the ctx passed at construction time is not the request-scoped context any caller can cancel or deadline. Any deployment where the search index build or watcher init fails transiently (DB hiccup, lock contention) now fails the whole NewResourceServer call — the process cannot start serving reads/writes that previously worked via the lazy-init retry path — and a long index build runs under a background context with no request deadline, blocking startup for its full duration.

[ADVISORY] Reordering init so search.init runs before initWatcher means events written between the search index build's snapshot read and watcher start are dropped from the index with no reconciliation. Tenants whose resources are modified during the (multi-second) index build window get stale search results until the index is rebuilt by RV check, because the previous ordering let the watcher buffer events while the index built; the diff adds no post-watcher-start RV reconciliation to close the gap, and the TODO in bleve.go acknowledges the RV check is not implemented.

[BUG] Moving Init() into NewResourceServer converts a per-request lazy failure into a hard construction/startup failure, and the diff adds no verification that all construction paths tolerate this. Any transient backend error during search index init (e.g., a short DB outage at startup) now makes NewResourceServer return an error and blocks the whole server from starting, whereas previously Init failure only failed individual requests and could be retried on the next request; during a rolling deploy, every instance that hits the failure window crashes on boot, turning a degraded search feature into a full outage.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the body of BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource key to run bleve.New on the same on-disk directory simultaneously, and the final cache write is last-write-wins. Concurrent initial searches for the same resource (previously serialized by the mutex held across the whole build) race on the same file-backed bleve directory, corrupting the on-disk index or leaking one index handle whose searchers read from a directory the winner later reopens; users get corrupt/empty search results until restart.

[BUG] The diff skips the sole integration test covering the instrumented resource server on postgres with a TODO, deleting postgres coverage of exactly the code paths this PR changes (Init-at-construction, watcher ordering) rather than fixing it. The lazy-Init-to-constructor-Init refactor, which changes startup behavior for the default production database, now has zero integration coverage on postgres in CI; a postgres-only Init failure (e.g., schema or stats query incompatibility) ships unnoticed and every postgres deployment fails at startup.

[ADVISORY] The watcher is now started after search index initialization instead of before, and the diff contains no verification that no events are lost during the (potentially long) index build. Events written to the change log during index build are only picked up if initWatcher subscribes before init replays from the latest RV; if the index snapshot RV is captured before the watcher starts, writes landing between snapshot and watcher start are silently missing from the index until a full rebuild — search returns stale/missing dashboards with no error surfaced anywhere.

[ADVISORY] Eager Init() in NewResourceServer converts the previously per-request, sync.Once-guarded lazy initialization into a hard construction-time failure, changing the server's failure semantics from per-request errors to process-wide startup failure. Any embedder of NewResourceServer (tests, secondary server constructions, provisioning code) that could previously tolerate a failing Init at request time now gets a nil server; if the search index or watcher fails transiently during startup, the entire Grafana process fails to boot rather than serving degraded requests. This is a startup-semantics change shipped under a 'performance optimization' PR with no requirement in the stated intent.

[ADVISORY] Reordering init so search.init runs before initWatcher changes the index bootstrap/watch race window, with no stated requirement driving the reorder. Events written between the search index build snapshot and the watcher starting are now handled after the index already includes their resources, so handleEvent re-indexes already-indexed docs; conversely under the old order the gap was between watcher start and index build. The behavior change is not traceable to any requirement in the PR description, and if it was needed for correctness of a perf change, that invariant (no lost events, no missed dedup) is nowhere documented or tested.

[BUG] Narrowing the cacheMu critical section in BuildIndex removes the mutual exclusion that serialized concurrent index builds for the same key, so two concurrent calls now both run bleve.New on the same directory and race on the final b.cache[key] write. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource both execute; the loser's index object is silently discarded while its bleve file-backed directory may hold an open writer, and callers that received the discarded index via another path keep querying an index that will never receive updates — under-scoped for a 'performance' change whose new concurrency is neither required by the PR intent nor covered by any test in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The postgres skip with a 'TODO - fix this test for postgres in Drone' comment disables the only integration coverage of the storage server on postgres, and is not traceable to any requirement of the PR. Postgres is the primary production database for Grafana; this PR's changes to server initialization timing and search index startup now ship with zero postgres integration coverage, so a regression in exactly the paths this PR touches (Init in NewResourceServer, watcher ordering) on postgres CI is undetectable until it reaches production.

[ADVISORY] Init() is called from NewResourceServer with a context whose provenance is not established in this diff, and the per-handler Init removal means the request-scoped context previously used for tracing/timeout during lazy init is replaced by a single constructor-scoped context. Traces for the index-build/watcher startup now attach to whatever background context was available at construction rather than a request, and an init hang (e.g., slow search index build) has no request deadline or cancellation path, blocking NewResourceServer indefinitely during startup with no way to abort — a failure mode the old lazy-init design bounded per-request.

[BUG] Reordering init so the search index is fully built before initWatcher() starts creates a window where writes landing during the (potentially minutes-long) index build are never captured, leaving the search index permanently stale for those resources. The previous order started the watcher first so WrittenEvents were queued/consumed while the index built; now any Create/Update/Delete whose event fires during the build is never indexed (the event is consumed/skipped by the already-running searchSupport against an index built from a pre-event snapshot, or lost entirely), so search results silently omit or show stale versions of dashboards modified during startup — a degraded index with no error surfaced.

[BUG] Moving Init(ctx) from per-request lazy initialization into NewResourceServer converts a previously per-request/recoverable failure into a hard startup failure for the entire Grafana server process. If search index construction or watcher setup fails (e.g. transient DB issue or a bad index directory on disk), NewResourceServer now returns an error at startup and the whole process refuses to boot, where previously the server came up and served non-search requests while only the affected RPCs returned the init error. One flaky dependency at boot takes down all tenants.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test for the storage server is skipped in CI with only a 'works locally' TODO, so the changed startup/init path in this PR (NewResourceServer eager Init, reordered watcher/search init) has no postgres coverage in the pipeline. A green CI build never exercises the new eager-init construction against postgres, exactly the backend where init behavior differences (index build queries, watcher) most plausibly break; a production-only postgres regression in server startup ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] s.log.Info("search index initialized", ...) is placed after the goroutine-launching block but the duration/total-docs values are computed from the enclosing function, reporting 'initialized' at enqueue time rather than at completion of the async build. Operators reading logs see an 'index initialized' line with a duration that measures only the synchronous setup, while the actual build continues in the background goroutine started just above — misleading observability when diagnosing slow-startup or stale-search incidents.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.'), silently deleting the only CI coverage for the storage server on postgres without any accepted replacement. Regressions in unified storage server behavior on postgres will ship green in CI and only surface in customer environments running postgres; the PR titled 'performance optimizations' now has zero postgres CI validation of the storage server it restructures.

[BUG] Init moved from per-request lazy initialization to hard failure inside NewResourceServer, converting what were per-request errors (e.g., search index build failure) into a construction-time failure that prevents the server object from existing at all. Any deployment whose database or search index is temporarily unavailable at process start now fails to construct the resource server and blocks Grafana startup entirely, where previously the server constructed fine and served requests that retried Init — this is a semantic objective change (availability traded for startup strictness) with no acceptance criteria or fallback path in the diff.

[ADVISORY] Init order was silently changed so the watcher now starts after search index initialization instead of before, meaning events written during a long index build are no longer captured by a live watcher during the build window. Tenants with large dashboards/folders get a search index built from a snapshot while the watcher is not yet consuming events; writes issued between the builder's list snapshot and watcher startup are missing from the index until they are re-written, producing stale search results — the ordering change is undocumented and has no test.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer converts a per-request failure into a hard startup failure for the whole process. Any environment where the search index or watcher initialization transiently fails (e.g. backing store briefly unavailable at boot) now refuses to start Grafana entirely, instead of the previous behavior where only the affected requests errored; operators get a crash-looping pod during a rolling deploy where old code would have served Reads/Lists.

[BUG] Removing the build-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key to both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory (when size > FileThreshold), and the second one fails because the Bleve index path already exists. During server startup with parallel index builds (init previously held this lock across the whole build), a duplicate concurrent BuildIndex for a large namespace returns an error instead of an index, causing Init to fail and — combined with Init now being called from NewResourceServer — the whole ResourceServer constructor to fail; the previous code serialized this correctly.

[ADVISORY] Removing the per-request Init guard means any code path that obtains a *server without going through NewResourceServer (or before Init completes in a future refactor) now executes Create/Update/Delete/Read against an uninitialized store with no error gate. The per-request Init call was the only runtime invariant guaranteeing the store/watcher/search were ready before mutating data; if a new constructor or test helper bypasses NewResourceServer, writes silently proceed against uninitialized state instead of returning the previous initialization error, a latent trust-boundary regression rather than an active vulnerability in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The only test-file change in this diff disables the integration test for the resource storage server on postgres in CI, so the PR's central behavioral change (Init moved from every handler into NewResourceServer) is verified by no running test. CI goes green while the new constructor-time Init path — which now hard-fails server startup on any search-init error instead of failing per-request — is never exercised in Drone; a regression in startup-time init (e.g., the search index or watcher failing) surfaces only in production at server boot, not in any automated test run. Checked pkg/server/module_server_test.go — no other test in the diff references NewResourceServer, Init, or the removed per-handler init guards.

[ADVISORY] The diff reorders initialization so the search index is fully built before initWatcher() starts, and no test covers this reordering or its event-coverage consequence. Writes committed to the SQL backend while the (potentially long) index build runs are never seen by the watcher because it is not yet started; previously the watcher began first and could buffer/handle events during the build. Tenants with large datasets get an index missing documents written during startup, and search returns stale/absent results with no error. Checked pkg/server/module_server_test.go and the whole diff — no test exercises the init ordering or concurrent writes during startup.

[ADVISORY] Init failure in NewResourceServer returns a nil server with error, converting every previously per-request init failure into a constructor failure, with no test for the failure path. Any caller of NewResourceServer (e.g., module wiring in package server) that previously tolerated a lazily-initialized store now fails construction; if any call site ignores the error or the shared ctx used here is a background context detached from request lifetimes, startup semantics silently change. No test in the diff constructs a ResourceServer with a failing search init to verify the error propagates rather than panicking (e.g., on nil s.search or the s.diagnostics used by IsHealthy).

[ADVISORY] Lazy per-request initialization is replaced with eager initialization in NewResourceServer, converting any transient init failure (search index build, watcher start) into a hard startup failure. Operators of Grafana instances with large resource counts or a temporarily unavailable backing store (the search index init scans/writes documents and initWatcher dials the watcher) will see the whole server process fail to boot instead of serving degraded reads/writes as before; a previously per-request recoverable error is now a deploy-blocking crash loop. Additionally, any construction path that does not go through NewResourceServer (or future callers that skip the added Init call) hits nil/zero-value backends with no guard, since the defensive Init calls were deleted from all ten RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob).

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource key, so two callers race to write b.cache[key] and the loser's index is silently discarded while remaining open. getOrCreateIndex callers that miss the cache concurrently (e.g. an event handler and a background build during search.init) both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory for file-based indexes; the second bleve.New on a directory already open by another index instance fails or corrupts state, and the loser's built index (and its open file handle / mmap) is never closed — leaked file handles plus duplicate full-index builds per race, and the last writer wins so a build with a stale RV can overwrite a newer one in the cache.

[ADVISORY] Init is moved into NewResourceServer, converting every initialization failure (DB stats query, search index build, watcher start) from a per-request error into a hard construction-time failure that aborts startup. Operators of environments where an index build transiently fails (e.g. slow DB during a spike) now get a process that will not boot rather than a degraded-but-serving server; previously Init's sync.Once error was returned per request and could be retried by a later request after the transient condition cleared.

[ADVISORY] Reordering init so the search index fully builds before initWatcher starts means events written to the store while the (possibly minutes-long) search.init is running are never indexed, with no error or stale-count surfaced. Tenants with large indexes get a search index that is permanently missing every write that occurred during the build window; the new 'search index initialized' log reports total_docs as if the index were complete, so the partial index is reported as a success and no re-sync is triggered.

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Since this PR also changes resource server initialization timing (calling `s.Init(ctx)` inside `NewResourceServer` and removing per-RPC `Init` calls, plus reordering watcher vs search init), skipping postgres integration runs does reduce the chance of catching regressions in the areas touched. The claim that this is the *only* postgres integration coverage can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the coverage reduction for postgres in this test is verifiable and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init() is called from NewResourceServer with a context whose provenance is not established in this diff, and the per-handler Init removal means the request-scoped context previously used for tracing/timeout during lazy init is replaced by a single constructor-scoped context. Traces for the index-build/watcher startup now attach to whatever background context was available at construction rather than a request, and an init hang (e.g., slow search index build) has no request deadline or cancellation path, blocking NewResourceServer indefinitely during startup with no way to abort — a failure mode the old lazy-init design bounded per-request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` before returning (server.go), and all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This means initialization (including `s.search.init(ctx)` and watcher startup) will now use the constructor-scoped `ctx` rather than a request-scoped context, changing tracing/cancellation semantics. However, the diff does not establish what `ctx` is in `NewResourceServer`, so claims about it being a background context with no deadline/cancel can’t be fully verified from the diff alone; it’s still a concrete design/observability concern grounded in these changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering init so the search index is fully built before initWatcher() starts creates a window where writes landing during the (potentially minutes-long) index build are never captured, leaving the search index permanently stale for those resources. The previous order started the watcher first so WrittenEvents were queued/consumed while the index built; now any Create/Update/Delete whose event fires during the build is never indexed (the event is consumed/skipped by the already-running searchSupport against an index built from a pre-event snapshot, or lost entirely), so search results silently omit or show stale versions of dashboards modified during startup — a degraded index with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes init order in `(*server).Init`: search index init (`s.search.init(ctx)`) now runs before `s.initWatcher()` (was the reverse). This creates a plausible gap where change events occurring while the index is being built would not be observed if `initWatcher()` does not replay/catch up from a persisted cursor. However, the diff does not show how `initWatcher()` works (e.g., whether it replays events since a last RV) or how `search.init()` builds/records a consistent starting point, so the claimed “permanently stale”/“never captured” behavior cannot be verified solely from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Moving Init(ctx) from per-request lazy initialization into NewResourceServer converts a previously per-request/recoverable failure into a hard startup failure for the entire Grafana server process. If search index construction or watcher setup fails (e.g. transient DB issue or a bad index directory on disk), NewResourceServer now returns an error at startup and the whole process refuses to boot, where previously the server came up and served non-search requests while only the affected RPCs returned the init error. One flaky dependency at boot takes down all tenants.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from per-RPC lazy init to constructor-time init: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails (server.go: added block before `return s, nil`), while the per-request `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from many RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc). This verifiably changes failure timing/behavior from “errors surface on first RPC” to “constructor can fail and prevent server creation.” However, whether that is a *bug* vs an intentional fail-fast/availability tradeoff isn’t provable from the diff alone; it’s an architectural/operational concern grounded in this change, not a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test for the storage server is skipped in CI with only a 'works locally' TODO, so the changed startup/init path in this PR (NewResourceServer eager Init, reordered watcher/search init) has no postgres coverage in the pipeline. A green CI build never exercises the new eager-init construction against postgres, exactly the backend where init behavior differences (index build queries, watcher) most plausibly break; a production-only postgres regression in server startup ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a CI skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` ("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally."). In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and `Init` reorders initialization (search index init before `initWatcher`) while removing the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls from many handlers. With postgres integration coverage now skipped in CI, the pipeline will not exercise these new startup/init semantics against postgres, making the risk of an undetected postgres-specific init/startup regression a concrete, diff-grounded concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] s.log.Info("search index initialized", ...) is placed after the goroutine-launching block but the duration/total-docs values are computed from the enclosing function, reporting 'initialized' at enqueue time rather than at completion of the async build. Operators reading logs see an 'index initialized' line with a duration that measures only the synchronous setup, while the actual build continues in the background goroutine started just above — misleading observability when diagnosing slow-startup or stale-search incidents.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:s.(*searchSupport).init, the new log line `s.log.Info("search index initialized", ...)` is emitted immediately after the block ending with `}()` (which appears to be an async/closure launch just above) and after computing `end := time.Now().Unix()`. From the diff, the logged `duration_secs` is therefore measured only up to that point in init(), not necessarily until the background indexing work completes. That makes the "initialized" message potentially misleading for operators, but it’s an observability/logging semantics issue rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.'), silently deleting the only CI coverage for the storage server on postgres without any accepted replacement. Regressions in unified storage server behavior on postgres will ship green in CI and only surface in customer environments running postgres; the PR titled 'performance optimizations' now has zero postgres CI validation of the storage server it restructures.

[BUG] Init moved from per-request lazy initialization to hard failure inside NewResourceServer, converting what were per-request errors (e.g., search index build failure) into a construction-time failure that prevents the server object from existing at all. Any deployment whose database or search index is temporarily unavailable at process start now fails to construct the resource server and blocks Grafana startup entirely, where previously the server constructed fine and served requests that retried Init — this is a semantic objective change (availability traded for startup strictness) with no acceptance criteria or fallback path in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from per-request lazy Init calls to construction-time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, while the explicit `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob`. This does make init failures (e.g., `s.search.init(ctx)` or `s.initWatcher()`) prevent `NewResourceServer` from returning a usable server instance, which can tighten startup availability. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this is an incorrect behavior (it may be an intentional change to fail fast); it’s a substantive semantic/availability tradeoff that warrants explicit rationale/acceptance criteria, not a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init order was silently changed so the watcher now starts after search index initialization instead of before, meaning events written during a long index build are no longer captured by a live watcher during the build window. Tenants with large dashboards/folders get a search index built from a snapshot while the watcher is not yet consuming events; writes issued between the builder's list snapshot and watcher startup are missing from the index until they are re-written, producing stale search results — the ordering change is undocumented and has no test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes init order in `(*server).Init`: the watcher startup block was moved to after `s.search.init(ctx)` (see removal before and addition after in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`). That is a real, specific behavior change that could affect how concurrent writes during a potentially long index initialization are observed, but the claimed “missing from the index until re-written” outcome depends on details not shown here (e.g., how `initWatcher()` chooses its starting revision / whether `search.init` accounts for a catch-up window). So the ordering change is real and review-worthy, but the concrete data-staleness bug is not strictly provable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving Init from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer converts a per-request failure into a hard startup failure for the whole process. Any environment where the search index or watcher initialization transiently fails (e.g. backing store briefly unavailable at boot) now refuses to start Grafana entirely, instead of the previous behavior where only the affected requests errored; operators get a crash-looping pod during a rolling deploy where old code would have served Reads/Lists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization from request handlers into construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if init fails, and the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` (server.go). This does change failure mode from “server can be created but first RPC will fail with initErr” to “server creation fails and the process may fail to start”, which is an operational/architecture concern. However, the finding overstates that the previous behavior would have continued serving Reads/Lists: previously `Read` and `List` also called `s.Init(ctx)` and would have errored if init failed. So the core concern is grounded, but not all stated consequences are strictly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the build-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key to both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory (when size > FileThreshold), and the second one fails because the Bleve index path already exists. During server startup with parallel index builds (init previously held this lock across the whole build), a duplicate concurrent BuildIndex for a large namespace returns an error instead of an index, causing Init to fail and — combined with Init now being called from NewResourceServer — the whole ResourceServer constructor to fail; the previous code serialized this correctly.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` previously held `b.cacheMu` for the entire build (including the `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on-disk creation path). The diff removes that wide lock and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. If `BuildIndex` is called concurrently for the same `key` and `size > FileThreshold`, both goroutines can race to create the same directory via `bleve.New(dir, ...)`, which is a correctness issue (second create may fail because the path already exists / is partially initialized). Separately, `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` inside `NewResourceServer` and returns the error, so any such init-time build error can now fail construction rather than being deferred until first request. The exact concurrency at startup isn’t shown in the diff, but the removal of the build-wide lock objectively makes same-key concurrent builds unsafe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the per-request Init guard means any code path that obtains a *server without going through NewResourceServer (or before Init completes in a future refactor) now executes Create/Update/Delete/Read against an uninitialized store with no error gate. The per-request Init call was the only runtime invariant guaranteeing the store/watcher/search were ready before mutating data; if a new constructor or test helper bypasses NewResourceServer, writes silently proceed against uninitialized state instead of returning the previous initialization error, a latent trust-boundary regression rather than an active vulnerability in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the per-request `s.Init(ctx)` guard from many RPCs (`Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `PutBlob`, `GetBlob`) in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` once inside `NewResourceServer(...)` (returning error if init fails). This does shift the runtime invariant: previously any caller invoking methods on a `*server` would trigger initialization and see an init error; now correctness depends on construction via `NewResourceServer` (or some other explicit init call). The diff itself does not show any alternative constructor/test helper that bypasses `NewResourceServer`, so it’s not a verifiable defect here, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/architecture concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test-file change in this diff disables the integration test for the resource storage server on postgres in CI, so the PR's central behavioral change (Init moved from every handler into NewResourceServer) is verified by no running test. CI goes green while the new constructor-time Init path — which now hard-fails server startup on any search-init error instead of failing per-request — is never exercised in Drone; a regression in startup-time init (e.g., the search index or watcher failing) surfaces only in production at server boot, not in any automated test run. Checked pkg/server/module_server_test.go — no other test in the diff references NewResourceServer, Init, or the removed per-handler init guards.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` in `pkg/server/module_server_test.go`, with a comment that it’s not working in Drone. In the same PR, `Init` is moved to constructor-time (`NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure) and the per-handler `Init(ctx)` guards are removed across many RPCs in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`. Disabling this integration test for postgres in CI is a concrete, diff-grounded coverage/regression-risk issue for the new startup-time init behavior, even if other environments/dbs may still exercise it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff reorders initialization so the search index is fully built before initWatcher() starts, and no test covers this reordering or its event-coverage consequence. Writes committed to the SQL backend while the (potentially long) index build runs are never seen by the watcher because it is not yet started; previously the watcher began first and could buffer/handle events during the build. Tenants with large datasets get an index missing documents written during startup, and search returns stale/absent results with no error. Checked pkg/server/module_server_test.go and the whole diff — no test exercises the init ordering or concurrent writes during startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization inside `(*server).Init`: search index init now runs before `initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`, moved “Start watching for changes” block to after `s.search.init(ctx)`). That change is real and nontrivial, and the only test change is a DB-type skip in `module_server_test.go`, with no new coverage for init ordering or concurrent write behavior. However, the specific claim that writes during a long `search.init` are “never seen”/will definitively cause missing docs is not directly provable from the diff alone (it depends on how the watcher establishes its starting point / event log semantics, which aren’t shown). So this is a concrete, diff-grounded risk/coverage gap rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init failure in NewResourceServer returns a nil server with error, converting every previously per-request init failure into a constructor failure, with no test for the failure path. Any caller of NewResourceServer (e.g., module wiring in package server) that previously tolerated a lazily-initialized store now fails construction; if any call site ignores the error or the shared ctx used here is a background context detached from request lifetimes, startup semantics silently change. No test in the diff constructs a ResourceServer with a failing search init to verify the error propagates rather than panicking (e.g., on nil s.search or the s.diagnostics used by IsHealthy).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, while per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob`. This converts what was previously lazy/per-request initialization (and potential per-request init failure) into a constructor-time failure, which can affect call sites that previously constructed the server successfully and only failed on first use. The finding’s point about missing coverage is also diff-grounded: no new test is added to validate the constructor failure path when `Init` (e.g., `s.search.init(ctx)` or `s.initWatcher()`) fails. Some specifics in the finding (e.g., exact ctx being background/detached, or panic on `nil s.search`) aren’t verifiable from the shown diff, but the core concern is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Lazy per-request initialization is replaced with eager initialization in NewResourceServer, converting any transient init failure (search index build, watcher start) into a hard startup failure. Operators of Grafana instances with large resource counts or a temporarily unavailable backing store (the search index init scans/writes documents and initWatcher dials the watcher) will see the whole server process fail to boot instead of serving degraded reads/writes as before; a previously per-request recoverable error is now a deploy-blocking crash loop. Additionally, any construction path that does not go through NewResourceServer (or future callers that skip the added Init call) hits nil/zero-value backends with no guard, since the defensive Init calls were deleted from all ten RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (server.go around the new `err := s.Init(ctx)` block), while all the defensive per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from many handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). This means transient init failures (e.g., `s.search.init(ctx)` or `s.initWatcher()`) that previously could fail on a request and potentially succeed on a later request without killing the process will now prevent server construction entirely. That is a concrete operational/architecture concern grounded in the diff, though not a provable correctness defect by itself. The additional claim about other construction paths bypassing `NewResourceServer` is plausible but not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource key, so two callers race to write b.cache[key] and the loser's index is silently discarded while remaining open. getOrCreateIndex callers that miss the cache concurrently (e.g. an event handler and a background build during search.init) both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory for file-based indexes; the second bleve.New on a directory already open by another index instance fails or corrupts state, and the loser's built index (and its open file handle / mmap) is never closed — leaked file handles plus duplicate full-index builds per race, and the last writer wins so a build with a stale RV can overwrite a newer one in the cache.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously took b.cacheMu for the entire function and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This diff-grounded change removes mutual exclusion during index creation (`bleve.New(dir, ...)` / `bleve.NewMemOnly(...)`) and the build process, so concurrent callers can build the same `key` in parallel and then race on the final cache write (last-writer wins). There is no code here to close/dispose an index instance that loses the cache race, so the "loser" index can remain open/leak resources. For file-backed indexes, parallel `bleve.New` on the same directory is plausibly unsafe and can fail or cause inconsistent state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init is moved into NewResourceServer, converting every initialization failure (DB stats query, search index build, watcher start) from a per-request error into a hard construction-time failure that aborts startup. Operators of environments where an index build transiently fails (e.g. slow DB during a spike) now get a process that will not boot rather than a degraded-but-serving server; previously Init's sync.Once error was returned per request and could be retried by a later request after the transient condition cleared.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization to construction-time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (server.go `NewResourceServer`), and the per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from many methods (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This changes behavior from “process can start and requests may fail until init succeeds” to “process/server construction fails and startup aborts if init fails”, which is a real operational/architecture concern. However, the finding’s claim that later requests could retry after a transient failure isn’t supported by the diff because `Init` uses `s.initOnce.Do(...)` and stores `s.initErr`, so initialization would not be retried after the first failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reordering init so the search index fully builds before initWatcher starts means events written to the store while the (possibly minutes-long) search.init is running are never indexed, with no error or stale-count surfaced. Tenants with large indexes get a search index that is permanently missing every write that occurred during the build window; the new 'search index initialized' log reports total_docs as if the index were complete, so the partial index is reported as a success and no re-sync is triggered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly reorders `server.Init` so `s.search.init(ctx)` runs before `s.initWatcher()` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go). Since indexing updates appear to be driven by events (`handleEvent(ctx, evt *WrittenEvent)` in search.go) and the watcher is what “Start[s] watching for changes”, this change creates a real risk that writes occurring while `search.init` is building the index won’t be observed by the watcher. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify that `search.init`/`BuildIndex` fails to account for concurrent writes (e.g., via a consistent snapshot or a last-RV catch-up), so the claim that events are “never indexed” and the index is “permanently missing” those writes isn’t strictly provable here. The added success log (`search index initialized ... total_docs ...`) could indeed be misleading if such a gap exists, but the existence of the gap depends on unseen implementation details.
